subject: environmental-science
title: Cycles & Systems: The Nitrogen Cycle
welcome_lead: Nitrogen is the main gas in our air — and plants can't use most of it.
meta_desc: KS3 environmental science: nitrogen cycle, bacteria, fertilisers.
final_note: Soil bacteria are tiny heroes of farming.

concepts.def: Gas making up about 78% of the air.
Bacteria turning N2 gas into useful nitrates.
Nitrogen form plants can take from soil.
Plants like peas hosting nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

walkthroughs.body_html: About 78% of the air is nitrogen gas. But plants can't use it directly — it needs to become nitrate first.
Special nitrogen-fixing bacteria in soil and in legume roots turn N2 into nitrate. Plants then make proteins from nitrate.
Farmers add fertilisers to boost crops. Too much can wash into rivers and cause algae blooms — a problem called eutrophication.

mcqs.q: Why is atmospheric nitrogen unavailable to most plants directly?
options: N2 has a strong triple bond that most organisms cannot break.
They reflect sunlight back to Earth.
Because plants only use carbon.
Because plants cannot reach high enough to access it.
